title: Jurisdiction in International Law: Territoriality, Nationality, Universality, and Extraterritorial Reach
description: This article explains jurisdiction as legal competence in international law, including prescriptive, adjudicative, and enforcement jurisdiction; territoriality; subjective and objective territoriality; nationality; corporate nationality; passive personality; the protective principle; universal jurisdiction; extraterritorial reach; the Lotus principle; immunities; human-rights jurisdiction; maritime and digital jurisdiction; enforcement abroad; sanctions; and the relationship between jurisdiction, sovereignty, and global power.
primary_source_types: Permanent Court of International Justice materials
United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea materials
